title: Writing Ella at Duke's Place and Norman Granz stealing Jones from Duke
summary: Duke asked Jones to write with him for the Ella Fitzgerald album while Strayhorn was ill, but Granz hired him for Ella.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah, I think that had quite a bit to do with it. And when he called me to come out here to do an album called, 'Ella At Duke's Place,' Ella Fitzgerald, you know?
Uh-huh.
I was sitting home and he was out -- he was working out here on the West Coast at that point, and he says, 'I would like for you to come out and write some scores with me.' Just like that.
Was that the first time he asked you to write with him?
I think so.
That was in the middle '60s, as I remember.
I think so.
1965, I think that was, wasn't it?
I guess so, because I joined Ella -- the setup was for me to go with Ellington, because Strayhorn was quite sick at that point, you know.
Uh-huh.
And to pick up Strayhorn's slack, you know, so Duke wouldn't have too much on his back, you know? But as luck, or whatever you want to call it, would have it, Norman Granz stole me away from him.
You think that was lucky?
Financially, yes.
(Laughter)
So -- but we all wound up being booked together. It was an act, you know, Ella and Duke.
Uh-huh.
So we were all together anyway. And then Europe, Jazz at the Philharmonic, or even this last album that I liked quite a bit, "The Greatest --," what was it, "The Greatest Jazz Concert?"
Uh-huh.
And Norman gave me one of those albums, and I thought it came out very well.
Yeah, I did too.
You know, because I'd forgotten that we'd done all that work in so many different places. Some of it was from Europe, some of it was from here, you know, and --
